title: Last questions from the unreviewed screens

steps.path: Any grid of things you can open or install
steps.headline: Is this the chip-style card you asked for?
steps.notice: Your note: keep today's chip look for "Likely safe" and the author, and make the footer details chips too.

variants.label: Chips (your pick)
variants.summary: Trust and author chips kept; the footer details as chips; name and tinted status on top.

steps.path: The conversation cards in Resume, which also carry tag and done buttons
steps.headline: With the date top right, where do a card's tag and done buttons go?
steps.notice: You chose the date top right. Resume's cards already use that corner for two small buttons.
steps.risk: "Icons on hover" leaves phones and touchscreens without the buttons, because there is no hover there.

variants.label: Icons bottom right
variants.summary: Date top right; the two buttons at the end of the details line.

variants.label: Icons on hover
variants.summary: Date top right; the buttons appear beside it only under the pointer.

variants.label: Icons keep the corner
variants.summary: Buttons stay top right; on these cards the date joins the details line.

steps.path: Ctrl+` or the terminal button in the header
steps.headline: Should the terminal keep its plain look or get the app's framing?
steps.today: The terminal view is a plain text area in the app window: white or dark background, monospace text, the command line at the bottom in a thin outlined box.
steps.problem: It follows none of the new rules (no card, no header), but it is a real terminal where text alignment matters, so framing it could get in the way.
steps.proposal: Either keep it plain on purpose and name it as an exception in the guide, or give it a light frame: the theme's card corner, a thin border and the same padding as chat.

options.label: Keep it plain
pros: Nothing changes; the terminal stays a terminal.
cons: Looks unlike the rest of the app.

options.label: Light frame
pros: Matches the chat view beside it.
cons: A little less room for text; a new look for a tool people know well.
